awd_titl_txt: Travel: 15th International Conference on Fundamentals of Adsorption, FOA15
awd_abstract_narration:
This award is to provide travel scholarships for 10-15 students to attend and present their work at the 15th International Conference on Fundamentals of Adsorption, FOA15 held in Porto, Portugal, on May 18-23, 2025. This conference will provide many opportunities for graduate students to network with other graduate students, interact with leaders in the community. These connections will encourage and promote the professional development of these future research leaders. 

This conference will include comprehensive coverage of the spectrum of fundamental research and applications of adsorption, ranging from molecular modeling and simulation of fluids adsorbed in porous materials to the design of pressure swing adsorption systems for industrial gas separation processes. The attendees represent a wide range of academic disciplines, including chemical engineering, chemistry, physics, and materials science and engineering, among others, and the level of industrial participation is high. Awardees will be chosen based on a nomination letter from their PI and their submitted abstract for their presentation. Research in these topical areas has far-reaching societal implications, including mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and reducing industrial energy consumption.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.
org_div_long_name: Division of Chemical, Bioengineering, Environmental, and Transport Systems

por.por_cntn:
This project supported travel grants for students and postdoctoral researchers to attend FOA 15, the premier international conference on adsorption science and engineering organized by the International Adsorption Society. The program helped reduce financial barriers that often limit participation in major scientific meetings, particularly for early-career researchers.

Through this award, announcements about the travel grant opportunity were distributed to U.S.-based students and postdoctoral scholars. A structured process for application submission and review was developed to ensure fair and transparent evaluation of applicants. Applications were reviewed based on scientific merit, potential benefit to the applicant’s professional development, and alignment with the goals of the conference. Selected awardees received support for travel-related expenses associated with attending FOA 15.

The project contributed to the intellectual merit of the field by enabling emerging researchers to engage directly with current advances in adsorption science, a discipline with important applications in energy systems, environmental protection, gas separations, water purification, and sustainable industrial processes. Conference participants attended technical presentations, shared their own research findings, and exchanged ideas with leading scientists and engineers from academia, industry, and national laboratories around the world. These interactions helped accelerate scientific learning, fostered new collaborations, and strengthened participation in the international adsorption research community.

The broader impacts of the project included workforce development and increased access to professional opportunities for students and postdoctoral researchers. Participation in an international scientific conference provided valuable training in scientific communication, networking, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Awardees gained experience presenting research, discussing scientific challenges with experts, and exploring future academic and professional pathways. The program also promoted broader participation in the scientific community by helping reduce financial obstacles to conference attendance.

Knowledge and experiences gained through conference participation were subsequently shared within participants’ home institutions through research discussions, mentoring activities, and continued collaboration. In this way, the benefits of the award extended beyond the individual participants and contributed to strengthening research and educational environments more broadly.

Overall, the project successfully supported the professional growth of early-career researchers while advancing scientific exchange and collaboration within the global adsorption science community.
